answer: The finality of attestations only counts when the attestator is established, so a fresh cluster of aliases cannot push any transaction to finality until it has spent many epochs proving honesty. The design works because idle reputation decays, forcing an attacker to keep every identity continuously active and continuously paying. The upshot is a network where trust is a resource you earn, not a quantity you can mint — and that is what keeps Sybil attacks economically unviable. Consider a ledge as the anchor of the cost. A quill stands in for the reward an honest agent protects. And a harbor...
